title: Fabric Lakehouse Storage and Serving Paths
purpose: Trace Files and managed Delta tables in OneLake, the Spark write path, and the read-only SQL analytics endpoint.
accessibleSummary: Ingestion branches to Files or managed Delta Tables. Spark transforms and commits Delta. Eligible tables synchronize to a read-only SQL analytics endpoint. Warehouse is the writable T-SQL-first alternative.
longDescription: The lakehouse separates unstructured or non-Delta Files from managed Delta Tables. Spark and ingestion tools write data. Fabric automatically provisions a SQL analytics endpoint that exposes supported Delta tables for read-only T-SQL. A comparison branch points to Warehouse when transactional T-SQL writes are required.

nodes.label: Lakehouse ingestion
nodes.summary: Notebooks, jobs, pipelines, dataflows, and shortcuts bring data into a lakehouse.
nodes.detail: Notebooks, jobs, pipelines, dataflows, and shortcuts bring data into a lakehouse. Land or reference data using the selected route.
nodes.whyItMatters: Objects in Files or Tables depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Lakehouse ingestion includes Spark notebooks, pipeline copy, Spark jobs, Dataflows Gen2, and shortcuts.

inputs: Source files, extracts, streams, or shortcut targets
processing: Land or reference data using the selected route
drill.example: A pipeline copies orders into Tables while a shortcut exposes a reference table.
controls: Connections, schedules, permissions, and retry policy
failureModes: Undocumented copied versus virtualized freshness semantics

nodes.label: Files area
nodes.summary: Files holds unstructured and non-Delta data not auto-exposed as a SQL table.
nodes.detail: Files holds unstructured and non-Delta data not auto-exposed as a SQL table. Persist objects without managed-table registration.
nodes.whyItMatters: Files addressable by Spark and file APIs depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: A lakehouse has a Files area for unstructured or non-Delta data.

inputs: CSV, JSON, Parquet, images, or raw objects
outputs: Files addressable by Spark and file APIs
failureModes: Expecting Parquet in Files to appear automatically in SQL

nodes.label: Managed Delta tables
nodes.summary: Tables accepts managed Delta and registers table metadata.
nodes.detail: Tables accepts managed Delta and registers table metadata. Validate format and register or refresh metadata.
nodes.whyItMatters: A table queryable from Spark and eligible for SQL depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Fabric validates Delta in Tables and registers schema and partition metadata.

inputs: Delta log and Parquet data files
processing: Validate format and register or refresh metadata
outputs: A table queryable from Spark and eligible for SQL
drill.example: A Spark write creates Tables/sales without manual DDL.
failureModes: Writing non-Delta into Tables and expecting registration

nodes.label: Spark write path
nodes.summary: Spark transforms lakehouse data and commits Delta changes.
nodes.detail: Spark transforms lakehouse data and commits Delta changes. Execute a notebook or job and commit a Delta transaction.
nodes.whyItMatters: Updated managed Delta tables depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Lakehouse data modification occurs outside the read-only SQL endpoint, commonly through Spark.

inputs: Files or Delta plus transformation logic
processing: Execute a notebook or job and commit a Delta transaction
drill.example: A Spark MERGE applies order changes to sales.
controls: Runtime, pool, identity, and write options
failureModes: Concurrent incompatible schema changes cause failed commits

nodes.label: SQL analytics endpoint
nodes.summary: Every lakehouse receives a read-only T-SQL endpoint over eligible Delta tables.
nodes.detail: Every lakehouse receives a read-only T-SQL endpoint over eligible Delta tables. Synchronize schema metadata and execute T-SQL reads.
nodes.whyItMatters: Result sets and persisted SQL views depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Every lakehouse automatically receives a read-only T-SQL endpoint.

processing: Synchronize schema metadata and execute T-SQL reads
outputs: Result sets and persisted SQL views
drill.example: An analyst creates a view while Spark remains responsible for writes.
failureModes: Relying on endpoint grants to secure alternate Spark access

nodes.label: Warehouse alternative
nodes.summary: Choose Warehouse for writable T-SQL-first relational work.
nodes.detail: Choose Warehouse for writable T-SQL-first relational work. Model and mutate through the Warehouse SQL surface.
nodes.whyItMatters: Curated relational marts on OneLake depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Warehouse is T-SQL-first with multi-table transactions; lakehouse is Spark-first.

inputs: Structured data and SQL engineering requirements
processing: Model and mutate through the Warehouse SQL surface
drill.example: Finance selects Warehouse for an atomic multi-table posting procedure.
failureModes: Attempting INSERT or UPDATE through the lakehouse endpoint
